biography.plain_text: Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said is Oman’s head of state and a member of the Al Bu Said dynasty. Educated in Oman, Lebanon and Britain, he built a public-service career in foreign affairs and heritage before succeeding Sultan Qaboos in 2020. His prominence is dynastic and governmental; no transparent evidence establishes an entrepreneurial fortune.

long_biography.plain_text:
Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said was born in Muscat and educated in Oman, Lebanon and Britain, including studies at Pembroke College, Oxford. He entered public service through the Foreign Ministry, rising to secretary-general, then served for nearly eighteen years as minister of heritage and culture. He also chaired the committee behind Oman Vision 2040, giving him a central role in long-term national planning before accession.

After Sultan Qaboos died, a sealed letter naming Haitham as successor was opened, and he became Sultan on 11 January 2020. His public position follows membership of the Al Bu Said dynasty and decades of government service. Public sources reviewed do not identify a distinct private business fortune, and the Oman Investment Authority explicitly manages assets of the Sultanate. Those sovereign holdings are therefore treated here as state assets, not as evidence of his personal wealth.
